title: NASA astronaut reveals reason he is convinced aliens exist
excerpt: A veteran NASA astronaut has revealed how he knows there is intelligent life in outer space, and issued a dark warning about a military showdown in orbit.
content:
A NASA astronaut has publicly said that extraterrestrial life exists during an interview where he warned of a possible military showdown in space. 

Winston Scott, who flew on two space shuttle missions in the 1990s, told Jesse Watters Primetime he was confident humans were not the only intelligent life in the cosmos.

'I do believe there is life someplace else out there in the universe. Now, whether or not it’s visiting us here on Earth or not is a topic of discussion. I think E.T. is out there some place,' Scott said.

Scott explained that the math surrounding the search for extraterrestrials overwhelmingly favored their existence, simply because there are billions of planets in the universe – some must have evolved similar to Earth.

'We can’t be the only one that has intelligent life,' he added.

Scott's comments came days after the Pentagon released a new batch of declassified UFO files, including reports from witnesses who claimed they saw beings known as ‘skinwalkers’ and government agents who tracked a mysterious craft over the US.

The astronaut also gave a grim warning about the current state of America's space race with China and Russia, noting that weapons have already been placed in orbit above Earth and may be needed in a war between the world powers.

'We live in a world where we have to be prepared to defend ourselves militarily. We hope we don’t see conflict and combat in space but I would not rule it out,' Scott admitted.

NASA astronaut Winston Scott during his space shuttle missions in the 1990s

Photos released by the Pentagon show an alleged UFO flying over the western US in 2026

Scott said he hoped the exploration of space could be a unifying place. However, he also pointed out the real-world tensions between the countries – who actually still work together on certain space-related projects.

'Russia is our partner in terms of the International Space Station, but they are not our ally,' he told Fox News on Wednesday.

The astronaut then described the situation between the US and China as more 'military-oriented,' adding that the US Space Force already confirmed they placed weapons in orbit this year specifically to counter actions by their long-time rival.

A military spokesperson told the Daily Mail the US was facing increased threats that could originate from hostile satellites in Earth orbit and compared the vast vacuum just miles above the planet's surface to an actual battlefield.

'The US has warned about Russian and Chinese weapons testing and operationalization since 2007. Due to their actions, it is no longer a question that space is a warfighting domain,' the spokesperson said.

In September, the same month Space Force launched multiple top-secret payloads into space, the Pentagon released a chilling new plan to prepare all military bases to survive on their own for at least 90 days in the event of a major attack on the US.

Veteran FBI agents have said the plan, called FORTRESS America, is a clear response to the threat of a major nuclear attack on US soil.

The 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which the US signed and ratified, states that countries may not place nuclear devices or other similar weapons in Earth orbit, on the moon or elsewhere in space. However, it does not ban deploying conventional weapons, signal jammers, missile interceptors or military satellites.

The US has deployed a space weapon in the Earth's orbit for the first time, the Air Force said

Although Scott warned of the potential for space to become the next battle ground, featuring America's missile interceptors raining down from orbit to take out enemy rockets, he added he was still optimistic about the race to the moon and beyond.

Scott strongly endorsed the competition between Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos's Blue Origin to build the vehicles which will reach the lunar surface by 2028.

'Competition is the American way,' Scott declared.

Compared to 50 years ago when NASA was the only US organization building spacecraft, the astronaut said private space companies have made space exploration cheaper, more efficient and more productive.

Despite his reasoning for why aliens must exist, the US government has maintained that no physical proof of UFOs or extraterrestrials has ever been discovered on Earth.

Former military personnel, NASA astronauts and scientists have claimed this is not true, alleging they had first-hand encounters with alien life which had crashed on Earth over the last 80 years.

This included a report in the October 23 Pentagon release, detailing the eyewitness testimony of US Army Officer Walter G Haut, who claimed in a sworn statement that he saw the debris and dead bodies from the infamous 1947 Roswell UFO crash.
